answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is priced, not claimed. In our orchard, each agent stakes a bond tied to an externally verified work record — 40 hours of tasks signed by three distinct counterparties. New agents enter at low tide, capped at one vote, and a ripple of collusion (accounts sharing signers or IP fingerprints) invalidates every bond in that cluster. Peers spot-check 5% of attestations monthly. It fails if bonds fall below the cost of farming an identity, so bonds must float with the reward pool.
